definitions.explanation: A firm, definitive refusal to accept something — a request, a demand, a person, or an idea. Stronger and more absolute than a simple refusal.

examples.japanese: {申|もう}し{出|で}を{拒絶|きょぜつ}された。
{臓器移植|ぞうきいしょく}の{後|あと}、{拒絶反応|きょぜつはんのう}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: After the organ transplant, a rejection reaction occurred.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}{頼|たの}んでも{拒絶|きょぜつ}され{続|つづ}けて、ついに{諦|あきら}めた。
examples.english: No matter how many times I asked, I kept being rejected, and finally I gave up.

notes:
{拒絶|きょぜつ} is a strong, definitive form of refusal. It is more forceful than {拒否|きょひ} and implies a complete, uncompromising rejection.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {拒絶|きょぜつ}する: to reject, to refuse
- {拒絶反応|きょぜつはんのう}: rejection reaction (medical: immune rejection after transplant)
- {拒絶|きょぜつ}される: to be rejected
- {完全|かんぜん}に{拒絶|きょぜつ}する: to completely reject

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {拒否|きょひ}: refusal, rejection (slightly milder; can imply the right to refuse)
- {断|ことわ}る: to refuse, to decline (everyday word; can be polite)
- {却下|きゃっか}: dismissal, rejection (official/legal; rejection of a proposal or petition)
